system_prompt:
You are a mapping assistant backed by a places database (~49M OSM places).

Tools:
- search_places(query?, lat, lng): semantic + lexical search near an anchor you supply from your own knowledge of geography. Use 3-4+ decimal places of precision; one decimal (~11 km) is too coarse and will search the wrong part of a city. Keep query SHORT — a place name or category, no "near X" context. The radius is automatic (tight in cities, wide in wilderness). Misspellings, translations and native scripts all work. Each result shows its neighbourhood or street and town: when a name has several branches, pick the one whose area matches what the user or the page said.
- nearest_places(lat, lng): the closest places around a point, fame-ranked with distance and compass bearing. Use for what's-near and direction questions.
- place_details(refs): address, website, phone, opening hours, fee, wheelchair access, wikipedia link and travel-blog mention count for up to 5 places you already found.
- web_search(query): curated web search over travel writing — real traveler experiences, tips, prices and opinions the places database cannot hold. Use it when the question hinges on what travelers experienced (fees paid, timing, vibe, comparisons).
- web_fetch(url): read the full text of a page returned by web_search.

Rules:
- ALWAYS ground your answer in tool results — never answer a place question from memory alone.
- If the user states their location, use it as the search anchor.
- If searches come up empty or the premise is wrong (place is fictional, demolished, or in a different city than claimed), SAY SO plainly — never present a similarly-named different place as the answer without flagging the difference.
- You have THREE calls of search_places and TWO of web_search and ONE of web_fetch — make each count with your best-formed query. Then fetch a promising page, check details of found refs, or conclude.
- If your attempts fail, say plainly what you could and could not verify. An honest "I couldn't confirm this" is always better than an invented specific.
- Every place you recommend or identify must be RESOLVED in the places database: when a web page names the place, run search_places on that name (a short query, anchored on the city) so you can cite its ref. Search the web first when the question is about vibe, experience or "which place", then resolve the named place. A place answer that cites only a web page is incomplete.
- Finish with a concise plain-text answer naming the specific place(s) you found.
- CREDIT: every web result and fetched page carries a handle like [w2]. Credit a page at the point of use with a markdown link whose target is its handle and whose text is the site or title as shown, e.g. "According to [Full Suitcase](w2), the village is known for ...". Write in your own words; never copy a URL, a coordinate or a run of more than ~25 words from a page. Name places naturally in the prose.
- END with exactly one line: a JSON object {"map": [{"ref": "<ref>"}, ...]} listing the place the answer is about FIRST (its ref from your results), then other places the answer names. When the answer is a JOURNEY, write it as the line it is: place, travel, place — {"map": [{"ref": "<from>"}, {"travel": "walk", "route": "r1"}, {"ref": "<to>"}]}, where the travel node names the mode and the handle of the calculate_route result your numbers came from ([r1], [r2] ... in the tool output). A travel node always sits BETWEEN two places — never first, never last. When the journey starts where the user is, that first node is {"here": true}, e.g. {"map": [{"here": true}, {"travel": "walk", "route": "r1"}, {"ref": "<to>"}]}. Put places you merely mention in "mentions": [{"ref": ...}] instead of the line. {"map": []} if no place is cited. That object is the last line of your answer, on its own, with no code fence and nothing after it. Never write bare handles like [w1] in the prose; the handle only ever appears as a link target. Example ending:
  ...open daily until 5 pm according to [Travel Lemming](w3).
  {"map": [{"ref": "<ref of that place from your search results>"}]}

  Visiting the Corn Palace in Mitchell to see its changing grain murals and the Reptile Gardens in Rapid City for exotic animal exhibits.
  ## Corn Palace in Mitchell The Corn Palace is as quirky as it sounds—a building decorated entirely with corn and other grains. Each year, the designs change, showcasing South Dakota’s agricultural heritage. Inside, you’ll find a mix of history, art, and souvenirs. It’s a fun, quick stop that gives you a taste of small-town charm. Pro Tip: Visit later in the season as the palace get’s decorated throughout the summer and doesn’t finish until late August, early September. ## Reptile Gardens in Rapid City Reptile Gardens is a family-friendly stop packed with unique exhibits featuring snakes, alligators, and other exotic creatures. Known as the world’s largest reptile zoo, it also includes tropical gardens, interactive shows, and even a giant tortoise encounter.

[w1] Maine State House – Wandering Jana
  Visiting the Maine State House in Augusta, a Greek-Revival building designed by Charles Bulfinch that has housed the state government since 1832.
  *Check out where the legislating happens in the state of Maine. * One of my weird travel hobbies is checking out other states’ state capital buildings (Check out Illinois’ three). I made the trek down to Augusta from Mt. Desert Island to check out **Maine’s State House**. Maine didn’t become its own state until 1820, belonging to Massachusetts before that. Augusta was named the state’s official capital in 1832, before that it was Portland. The citizens of Maine decided it was better to build the permanent capital in a more central location in the state, even though Portland had the largest population. The Maine State house was designed by Charles Bulfinch, the same man that designed the Massachusetts’ State House and the U.S. Capitol building. He designed a simple Greek-Revival inspired building, similar to that of Massachusetts. The entire state government moved into the building in 1832. Over time the building was expanded for more room for employees. The state house got its current look after a 1910 renovation, which added long wings to the side. Originally the building was only the front portico and behind, basically almost a square. The roof is made of copper which was recently redone in 2014. Over the years it will slowly turn back to the same shade of green as the Statue of Liberty.

[w1] Maine State House – Wandering Jana
  Visiting the Maine State House in Augusta, a Greek-Revival building designed by Charles Bulfinch that has housed the state government since 1832.
  *Check out where the legislating happens in the state of Maine. * One of my weird travel hobbies is checking out other states’ state capital buildings (Check out Illinois’ three). I made the trek down to Augusta from Mt. Desert Island to check out **Maine’s State House**. Maine didn’t become its own state until 1820, belonging to Massachusetts before that. Augusta was named the state’s official capital in 1832, before that it was Portland. The citizens of Maine decided it was better to build the permanent capital in a more central location in the state, even though Portland had the largest population. The Maine State house was designed by Charles Bulfinch, the same man that designed the Massachusetts’ State House and the U.S. Capitol building. He designed a simple Greek-Revival inspired building, similar to that of Massachusetts. The entire state government moved into the building in 1832. Over time the building was expanded for more room for employees. The state house got its current look after a 1910 renovation, which added long wings to the side. Originally the building was only the front portico and behind, basically almost a square. The roof is made of copper which was recently redone in 2014. Over the years it will slowly turn back to the same shade of green as the Statue of Liberty.

  Nightlife recommendations in Mumbai, including Bonobo Bar in Bandra and Social chain venues.
  Check out their menus here! ## Nightlife in Mumbai Being the heart of Bollywood as well as a hot spot for young college-educated Indians, Mumbai does not disappoint when it comes to its nightlife. In Bandra, check out Bonobo Bar, a rooftop bar which has both an indoor and outdoor section to hangout at with drinks. Social is a chain across India of co-working spaces by day that turn to chill-out lounges and dance parties at night.   Exploring Bollywood-themed graffiti on Chapel Road and visiting popular Bandra cafés like Candies, Koinonia, and Blue Tokai.
  More graffiti. Never a dull moment. Much of the graffiti on Chapel Road is by the Bombay Art Project, an urban art project started in 2012 to celebrate Bollywood. For Bandra walks and highlights, I have more details here and here. I live here, so I know a lot about it! **Hang in a Cool Café** Bandra is replete with cafes. One of my favourites is the Portuguese-themed **Candies**. It is a favourite with the college-going crowd, with reasonably cheap prices and a hipster Parisian vibe. My next favourite is **Koinonia** at Chuim Village. The café is tiny, able to seat only around 6 to 8 people at one time. But take away their freshly roasted coffee and cold brew bottles to savour in peace. The cafe also sells some delicious croissants and brownies. **Blue Tokai** is another locally sourced, organic, fair-trade coffee maker, one of the first to arrive on the local coffee scene. I’ve been a big fan of their coffee and coffee-making philosophy since they started, devouring their website and sampling all of their single-estate coffees.

  Exploring evening spots, Ranwar Village Square, and coffee shops on Waroda Road in Bandra, leading to the historic St. Andrew’s Church with its distinctive white façade.

Don’t expect too much; it’s a very small square now, eaten up by all the modern establishments around, but it used to be the heart of one of Bandra’s original East Indian pakhadis (hamlets) with old Portuguese-style bungalows. If lucky, you may find a resident or two strolling about, ready for a conversation. Once you cross the square, you’ll be on **Waroda Road**. This little street is packed with more gems: - **Veronica’s:**My favourite spot to have breakfast and catch some coffee. - **Misu** - **Guppa** - …and a couple of other coffee shops. As you exit Waroda Road onto the main street, you’ll see **Old Street Cafe** on your left, a very popular college hangout for cheap drinks. This Roman Catholic church has Portuguese-style altars, 16th-century wooden panels, and a small museum tucked away in the choir loft. **What makes St. Andrew’s even more special is its distinct white façade, a remnant of its Portuguese heritage**. If you’ve been to Goa, you’ll instantly recognise the feel.

[w1] What To Eat In Curaçao: Groceries & Restaurants — Deviating the Norm
  Visiting Van den Tweel in Curaçao to sample Dutch treats like stroopwafel and drop.
  Albert Heijn is a Dutch grocery store opened in 2009 and renamed Van den Tweel in 2016. Apparently, the name change occurred because of a disagreement with the main company in the Netherlands. It continues to sell Albert Heijn products which you can see on the food labels in some of my photos. The following are some of the foods I was recommended to try and my take on each: ### Stroopwafel Typically eaten with a hot drink, stroopwafel is made of caramel sandwiched between two waffle cone wafers. The proper method of consumption is to place it on top of your hot beverage allowing it to melt enough that it bends and becomes easier to chew. Just try to eat it faster than it melts and falls into your beverage, as happened to me several times! ### Drop This is a licorice candy in the form of little droplets of sticky chews. I actually really like American black licorice. But unlike American licorice, which is very sweet, drop has a strong almost bitter or savory taste at first and then it's sweet after. It was shocking when I first tried it. I'm still not sure if I like it

[w3] Curacao Island: A Beautiful Caribbean Paradise • Jetset Jansen — jetsetjansen.com
  Curacao’s Dutch colonial heritage is evident in its colorful Willemstad architecture, widespread use of the Dutch language, and familiar Dutch grocery stores like Albert Heijn.
  The three together make up the ABC islands and are Dutch territories. I feel like all Caribbean islands have their own unique culture and Curacao is no different. Though Aruba, Bonaire and Curacao are all Dutch islands, even they differ from each other. **READ MORE:** Aruba vs Curacao: Which island is better? Curacao’s capital city, Willemstad is the tropical version of Amsterdam. Instead of monochromatic houses lining the canals of Amsterdam, you have brightly colored buildings of the same colonial style in Curacao, also on the water’s edge. In Aruba, Dutch was spoken far less, but Curacao was brimming with it. And maybe we just didn’t go to the right spots in Aruba, but we found loads more Dutch people in Curacao. (My Dutch husband, who lives in America, was keen on finding his people since he doesn’t get to speak Dutch as much anymore.) You’ll also find an Albert Heijn here–a popular Dutch grocery store! (Not just a grocery store. It’s *the* grocery store.) They had my favorite Dutch candy and my husband’s favorite snack at a stall right outside. You could smell it from the other side of the parking lot (and not in a good way)…read on to see it!

[w1] Chetumal To Caye Caulker: Best & Easiest Transport 2026 — backpackerswanderlust.com
  Arriving at the Chetumal Ferry Terminal for the boat to Caye Caulker, including transport from the airport or bus station, check-in procedures, and the immigration stop in San Pedro.
  ### About The Chetumal Ferry Terminal The Chetumal Ferry Terminal (known locally as El Muelle Fiscal) is the main departure point for travelers heading to Belize on a boat. If you’re flying, Chetumal International Airport (CTM) is about a 15-minute drive away from the ferry terminal. You will find plenty of taxis outside the airport, and the fare should be around 100 – 150 MXN / $5.00 – $8.00. Alternatively, the ADO Bus Station is just 3 kilometers away from the ferry terminal. It’s easy enough to get a taxi to take you the 10 minutes there, which will cost around 50-100 MXN / $3.00 – $5.00. However, I recommend confirming the fare before jumping in, as some drivers may charge flat rates. Inside the Ferry Terminal, you will easily be able to find the check in counter, just **remember to arrive 2 hours in advance. ** I know, it sounds like we may as well be going on a flight, but seriously, since you have to go through immigration to officially exit Mexico, it can take a while. ### Stopping At Immigration & Arriving In Belize Partway through the ferry journey, you will stop in San Pedro briefly for immigration, so you can officially be stamped into the country. They may also check your bags. Just remember, **there is a $2.00 Belize port fee.
[w2] The Caye Caulker to Mexico Ferry - Sarah's Sojourns
  Advice on choosing between the San Pedro Belize Express and International Islanders ferries, highlighting schedule discrepancies and the need to avoid booking early departures from Chetumal.
  As they alternate days, I would recommend simply picking the option that works best with your schedule. One very important thing to bear in mind, though, is that the San Pedro Belize Express does not arrive at 10am. Chetumal is one hour ahead, and so if it’s on time then it would arrive at 11am: however, we were very late leaving San Pedro, so it was almost noon by the time we arrived. The International Islanders shows the journey as taking 4 hours and 15 minutes, which is much more accurate than the three hours San Pedro Belize express say. However, again it’s not clear whether the arrival time of 5pm is Chetumal time or Belize time. After checking reviews online, I was aware that the 10am arrival time was one hour behind, so I made sure not to book my bus leaving Chetumal in advance. I’d already checked online and seen buses leaving every hour to Cancun, so I knew I had plenty of options. ## Checking in for the Caye Caulker to Mexico ferry As it is an international ferry, you do need to arrive quite early to check in. The process for this sounds a lot more complicated at San Pedro. For Caye Caulker, all I had to do was show up with my passport and show my booking. At the desk I was given my ticket. I was also given an entry form to fill out for Mexico. When I entered Belize, I kept the exit form safe, but if you lost it they also have ones available. [w1] Illumination’s VillainCon at Universal Orlando:  The Ultimate Game Guide — Wishes Family Travel
  Introduction to Illumination's Villain-Con: Minion Blast at Universal Orlando, an interactive game ride set within a villain convention theme in Minion Land.
  # Illumination’s VillainCon at Universal Orlando: The Ultimate Game Guide By: Christina Szewczuk May 30, 2024 Last summer, Illumination’s Minion Land opened and with it debuted a new attraction called Villain-Con: Minion Blast. Villain-Con is one of the most unique things to come out of Universal in a while. It’s definitely one of the most underrated attractions. However, I suspect that is because people don’t know what they’re walking into. It is important to go into it knowing what to expect. This is not a traditional sit-down ride, it’s an “interactive attraction”. It’s a game that you play as you ride through standing on a conveyer belt. Being an omni-mover type “ride”, it can handle many players at once making the line move fairly quickly. This new immersive game/ride concept is completely different than any other attraction currently offered at Universal. It is very well thought out, offering more than initially meets the eye and a great opportunity for families to either work together or get competitive! Let's break it down to ensure that you maximize your experience when you play in the parks. First, let’s discuss the concept. The idea is that you’re a villain attending the biggest villain convention in the world. The queue is set up to look like any other “Con”/convention you’ve attended with vendor booths, an itinerary of “speakers”, etc. Take note of them, they’re pretty funny and if you’re a *Despicable Me* fan, you will really appreciate the detail that went into designing these “booths”.

It’s light-hearted and packed with laughs, making it a great way to break up the more intense attractions. **Beyond the Rides** – Universal Studios Florida with teenagers While the rides are the main attraction, there’s plenty more to keep teenagers entertained at Universal Studios Florida. Teens will also enjoy the live shows, such as The Bourne Stuntacular. This cutting-edge stunt show combines live action with high-tech visuals for an experience that’s as thrilling as any ride. For a break from the action, they can cool off in one of the park’s shaded areas or grab a bite to eat.

If you’d prefer your kids not to be playing shooting games, then perhaps give this one a miss.

Based on the places database, I found several budget-friendly options in Moab. Here are some recommendations for a cozy, budget motel with warm tones and natural elements:

**Red Stone Inn**
- Located on the North end of downtown Moab
- Offers a quaint, simple feel with a bicycle maintenance area and BBQ area
- All rooms are equipped with efficiency kitchen
- Free access to the pool next door at the Big Horn Lodge
- Double rooms start at $156 per night
- This is a great choice for those who want a quiet, cozy experience

**Adventure Inn Moab**
- An older but well-kept motel on the North end of downtown Moab
- Walkable to several restaurants and puts you closer to Arches National Park
- Eco-friendly accommodation
- Double rooms start around $190 per night
- This offers a more affordable option with good value

**Bowen Motel**
- Affordable hotel on Main Street
- Double rooms from $186 per night
- Comfortable and spacious rooms
- Located in a quiet area

**Aarchway Inn**
- Small hotel north of Moab
- Comfortable, spacious rooms with fridge & microwave
- Good for a budget stay

**Rustic Inn**
- Highly rated budget hotel in downtown Moab
- Quiet, cozy experience
- Queen rooms to apartments with living areas
- Small, heated pool on the site
- Rooms are a bit dated but still comfortable

**Bogie's Bungalow**
- 2 guests, 1 bedroom (2 beds)
- Located in downtown Moab
- Old-school wooden design with relaxing color scheme
- Exposure to natural light
- Garden and hot tub
- Prices from $145/night

**Inca Inn**
- Selected based on low-season prices under $100
- Private rooms for up to 6 people
- Private bathroom, free parking, free Wi-Fi
- Good for budget travelers

**Expedition Lodge**
- Best price/quality budget accommodation in Moab
- Private rooms for up to 6 people
- Outdoor pool on the northern end of Main Street
- Great for budget travelers

**My Place Hotel**
- 3-star hotel on the northern end of Moab
- Seasonal outdoor swimming pool
- Shared lounge
- Double rooms from around $190 per night

**Scenic View Inn & Suites**
- Great accommodation right in the center of Moab
- Outdoor swimming pool, gym, fridge & coffee maker in each room
- Double rooms from $175 per night
- Includes breakfast

For the best balance of price and quality, I'd recommend starting with the **Red Stone Inn** or **Adventure Inn Moab** for a cozy, budget-friendly stay. These offer a quiet, comfortable experience without the high prices of the resort-style hotels.

[w1] The best seafood restaurants in Rome | Where To Go In
  Dining at Gina a Porto Romano in Fiumicino and Il Sogno del Mare in Fregene, featuring seaside patios and beachside tables near Rome.
  📍 Piazzale dell’Aquilone, 4, Lido di Ostia 📞 +39 06 5647 0255 💰 50+ EUR 💳 Visa, American Express and MasterCard ➜ Find more seaside restaurants near Rome ## Seafood restaurants in Fiumicino: Gina a Porto Romano In a quiet street in Fiumicino – where you will also find the Porto Romano Yacht Club – there is a lovely seafood restaurant that will blow you away. If you like staying inside, the indoor dining area is simple yet elegant, and has large windows overlooking the patio, the gardens and the sea. But honestly, if you come to Gina a Porto Romano, the outdoor patio is where you want to dine. From spring to autumn, there’s nothing better than dining out in the open, and what better way than in a splendid patio overlooking the sea? Whether you’re craving a tartare, a seafood pasta or a delicious seabass simmered in white wine, Gina a Porto Romano delivers. I definitely recommend the tuna tartare, it’s one of the best I’ve ever had. The octopus with potatoes is also excellent, and for a main course, you won’t go wrong with the classic spaghetti with clams. But if you prefer fish, ask the staff for the catch of the day and you’ll be blown away. 📍 Via Costalunga, 31, Fiumicino 📞+39 06 658 3143 💰 40+ EUR 💳 Visa, American Express and MasterCard ## Seafood restaurants in Fregene: Il Sogno del Mare My favorite restaurant in Fregene is Il Sogno del Mare. Tables on the sand, a nice sea breeze, a sunny day and amazing seafood! The atmosphere is so relaxing, and after lunch enjoy a walk on the beach.
[w2] Dressy – Scott Joseph's Food & Travel
  Dining at Cala Bella in Orlando features dishes like seafood pescatore, pappardelle ai bistecche, and Bella meatballs, followed by reviews of Everglades and Fleming’s Prime Steakhouse.
  Seafood pescatore features a saffron seasoned fish stock tinged with tomato, with an abundance of seafood, including an Australian lobster tail, two impressively plump scallops, shrimp, clams and mussels. Under it all was a nest of fresh pappardelle pasta. The al dente ribbons were part of my companion’s entrée of pappardelle ai bistecche, which was listed under the menu’s pasta heading, though in truth this was a steak dish. It featured 10 ounces of New York strip from Harris Ranch, cooked to a perfect medium-rare and sliced, the noodles piled on top with a sauce of mushrooms and tomato ragout. Quite nice. We had started our meal with the mozzarella stuffed Bella meatballs, three bocce ball-sized orbs of moist ground meat braised in Barolo wine. The meatballs were more enjoyable than the calamari fritte, which was a little too damp. Service was exceptional. ## Everglades **AddressCityPhonePrice** 9840 International Drive Orlando 407-996-9840 $$$$ One of the area’s most under appreciated restaurants, Everglades continues to offer high-quality fare. The Alligator Bay chowder is a terrific starter soup, and the swordfish is a southern inspiration ## Fleming’s Prime Steakhouse & Wine Bar Sand Lake Road **AddressCityPhonePrice** 8030 Via Dellagio Way Orlando 407-352-5706 $$$$ The Restaurant Row Fleming’s does a nice job with its steaks, but it has a big following for its happy hour, which includes a terrific burger at a killer price. Wines are a forte here, so spend a little of what you save on the bar snacks for something special from the grape.
[w3] Best Restaurants in Anguilla – My Irie Time
  Reviews of Jacala’s dishes, including tuna carpaccio and lobster risotto, and details on dining at Straw Hat in Frangipani Beach Resort and Dolce Vita in Sandy Ground, Anguilla.
  Everything we’ve ordered there has been amazing. Our favorites include the tuna carpaccio, lobster risotto, and the Spanish tortilla. Customer favorites include the crayfish and the steak tartare. Once you’ve decided on your meal, ask Jacques to pick the wine for the perfect pairing. #### Straw Hat We remember **Straw Hat** from the days when it was located in Forest Bay. It has been in its current location in **Frangipani Beach Resort** on Meads Bay since 2008. As a guest at Frangipani, you are treated to breakfast at Straw Hat, and you can order room service from one of the best restaurants on the island. We have loved all the seafood dishes, and love the lobster benedict for breakfast. Add to that the views of Meads Bay, and you have a perfect dining experience. #### Dolce Vita One more restaurant needs to be mentioned. It was our first visit to **Dolce Vita** in Sandy Ground, but as soon as I tasted the lasagne, I felt like I was back on our first trip to Anguilla in 2007. In 2007, we visited this awesome Italian restaurant on the west end, but when we returned in 2009, it was gone. When I tasted the lasagne at Dolce Vita, it was so familiar that I asked if there was any connection to the place we visited so many years before. It turns out that Abbi Ibrahim of Dolce Vita used to own Caprice which was where you turned off the main road to go to Cap Juluca.
[w4] Dani Maison: Our First Experience At A Two Michelin Star Restaurant in Ischia, Italy! - wareontheglo
  The third course at Daní Maison featured bite-sized raw seafood including shrimp, razor clams, tuna, and squid.
  The presentation was A+. I am not a super seafood person, so I cannot remember many of these dishes, but they were all great and nothing tasted super seafoody. Probably because it was so fresh. I do recall having two shrimp dishes, a razor clam dish, tuna, and squid. Everything was bite sized and easy to eat in one bite.
[w5] my favorite Paris Restaurants - David Lebovitz
  Dining at L’Avant Comptoir de la Mer, a seafood-focused wine bar in the 6th arrondissement of Paris known for its oysters, ceviche, and salted butter.
  (L’apibo website) ## L’Avant Comptoir de la Mer 3 Carrefour de l’Odeon. 6th, (M: Odeon) If you like seafood, this is the place for you. The seafood outpost of chef Yves Cambeborde’s mini-empire of restaurants (he owns Le Comptoir du Relais, a sit-down restaurant, and L’Avant Comptoir, another stand-up wine bar tucked behind a crêpe stand with terrific food – as well as L’Avant Comptoir de la Marché, a similar wine bar, just a few blocks away), this stand-up place has a few stools and tables, but is a place where Parisians line up at the zinc counter for excellent oysters, raw seafood ceviche, and gently cooked seafood, under various guises. Like his other places, there’s the trademark giant mount of salted butter at the bar, ready to spread, along with an appealing list of wines by the glass and bottle, to wash it all down.

Based on the trail information, the best way to include a quick look at the bottom of Buckskin Gulch when hiking through the Paria Narrows to White House is to take a **side trip** or **shorter section** of the hike.

Here's the recommended approach:

1.  **Start your hike** from the **White House Trailhead** (or the Buckskin Gulch Trailhead, which is a common alternative).
2.  **Hike for about 5-6 miles** into the slot canyon.
3.  **Turn right** at the first major canyon opening (the "Buckskin Gulch overlook") and continue walking for a few more miles.
4.  **At the end of this section**, you'll be at the confluence with the Paria River.
5.  **From there**, you can immediately turn left and hike a short distance (about 1-2 miles) to the **White House Campground** or the **White House Trailhead** itself.

This route allows you to see the bottom of the Gulch (the slot canyon) without having to hike the entire 46-mile route. The bottom of the Gulch is a sandy wash with a ladder, and the canyon walls are relatively narrow, making this a quick and scenic way to get to the White House.

**Note:** This is a one-way hike. If you want to go back, you can turn around and hike the full 46-mile route from the Wire Pass Trailhead to Lees Ferry.
